Published online:
    September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: United States, with notable coverage of Japan, Australia, Europe, Singapore)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    A global bond selloff is driving US 10-year Treasury yields toward the critical 5% threshold, fueled by a "perfect storm" of oil prices surging past $100/barrel, persistent inflation fears, central bank hawkishness, and fiscal deficit concerns. The ECB has already hiked rates. Traders are now pricing a 72% probability of a Fed rate hike at next week's meeting, up sharply from 49% a week prior. Incoming US CPI data is the immediate key catalyst — a strong print is seen as likely to push 10Y yields decisively above 5%. Globally, bond markets from Australia to Japan to Europe are selling off in tandem.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the article is centrally focused on US Treasury yields approaching 5% and the rising probability of a Fed rate hike, set within a global bond selloff context)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 90 (overwhelmingly framed around rate hike expectations and the inflationary pressures driving them)
Probability of increase: 72% (explicitly cited from CME FedWatch tool as of the article date)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (briefly referenced only as a conditional scenario tied to a soft CPI print, not the dominant narrative)
Probability of holding: 28% (implied residual from the 72% hike probability)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (rate cuts are not discussed or implied anywhere in the article)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (strongly hawkish — 72% priced hike probability, 10Y yields at 4.97% and threatening to break 5%, oil above $100 sustaining inflation pressure, and imminent CPI data seen as a potential final trigger for the yield breakout)
